title: throughput-latency-price-tile-annotated-brief-aug10-2028
body:
Executive summary:

This brief documents a compact set of throughput vs. latency vs. unit-price trade experiments for our tiling/prefetch strategies across two representative model classes (long-context assistant-style; short micro-turn chat). The goal: give product and SRE teams an easy-to-scan map to decide tiling aggressiveness and pricing tier recommendations for conservative (p95-focused) and opportunistic (p50-focused) workloads.

Top-level findings:
- Aggressive tiling (longer slot aggregation, pre-warm affinity) improves amortized cost per token by 18-35% for sustained loads at the expense of p95 hovering +12–35 ms for short-turn interactions.
- For microburst chat (<= 16 tokens per turn, inter-arrival 50–300 ms), small-window tiling with KV-prefetch yields the best p95/price sweet spot. Large tiling hurts p95 by widening tail when cold-eviction occurs.
- For long-context generation (sequence lengths >= 1024), tiling with contextual prefetch + chunked KV cache recovers 22–28% of throughput vs naive per-request execution while maintaining p95 within product SLOs.

Methodology (short):
- Workloads: two synthetic distributions derived from production traces: MicroChat (mix of 1–12 token turns, high IAT jitter) and LongGen (20–2048 token sequences, sustained flow).
- Models: open-architecture 8B transformer (baseline_no_quant) and quantized 13B (q8_compat) to reflect typical hosted catalog pairs.
- Hardware: NVIDIA A100 40GB (core) and H100 80GB (edge-proxy cluster probe) with identical software stack and patched kernel-selection logic from tiling-bench v0.9.
- Metrics: p50/p90/p95 latency (ms), sustained QPS, tokens/sec, cost-per-token estimate (USD/token) using internal unit-cost model (GPU-hour amortized + infra egress).
- Runs: each point is median of 5 runs, 30m sustained windows for sustained points and 1m sampled bursts (1000 bursts) for microburst points.

Representative numeric table (high-level):

Mode | Model | Sloting | QPS | p50(ms) | p95(ms) | cost/token(USD*1e-6)
-----+-------+---------+-----+---------+---------+--------------------
MC   | 8B    | small   | 800 | 22      | 78      | 0.95
MC   | 8B    | large   | 950 | 28      | 105     | 0.72
LG   | 13B   | small   | 120 | 430     | 620     | 4.8
LG   | 13B   | large   | 150 | 465     | 695     | 3.7

Notes on the table: 
- MC (MicroChat) small = 40–80ms slot aggregation with aggressive KV reuse; large = 400ms slot with multi-session coalescing.
- LG (LongGen) small = chunk size 128 tokens; large = chunk size 512 tokens with prefetching.

ASCII sparkline (p95 vs QPS, MicroChat 8B, small->large):
QPS 200 400 600 800 1000
P95  48  58  68  78  102
Spark: ▂▂▃▅█

Interpretation and actionable guidance:
1) Default hosted API tier (general purpose): ship with "balanced-tiling" (slot=120ms, chunk=128) as conservative default. This preserves p95 within typical app SLOs while saving ~20% cost for sustained workloads.
2) Low-latency SDK path: expose a "micro" knob that forces small-slot tiling + immediate dispatch; recommended for chat UIs where p95 matters more than raw cost.
3) Dedicated capacity: offer a "tiling-optimized" reservation (long-slot aggregation, reserved KV memory) which we can price at ~15% discount vs base reserved price because amortized unit-cost improves at scale.
4) Private deployments: include a best-practice config snippet in the onboarding template that sets chunk_size according to mean sequence length (heuristic: chunk= min(512, mean_seq*1.5)).

Risk and caveats:
- Cold eviction regimes: large-slot strategies perform poorly when eviction churn is high. For customers with spiky, low-reuse sessions, large tiling can increase tail latency dramatically (up to 2x p95 in pathological cases).
- Model variance: quantized variants show slightly better cost numbers, but p95 sensitivity to kernel selection increases: ensure kernel fallback paths are warm.
- Measurement bias: our cost/token model assumes 70% utilization during sustained windows; lower utilization regimes will reduce the observed cost savings.

Diagnostic charts (text-first) to include in collateral: 
- Heat grid: x-axis: slot length (ms) 40..400, y-axis: mean seq len buckets. Cells: relative cost saving (%) and delta p95 (ms). Example cell entry: [+18% save, +28ms p95].
- Waterfall: per-token breakdown: compute | memory | scheduling | network. The compute slice shrinks with tiling, but scheduling/network may increase marginally.

Example heat excerpt (rows=bucketed mean_seq, cols=slot_ms):
mean_seq
16  |  +12%/+8ms  | +9%/+12ms  | +6%/+22ms  | +2%/+48ms
128 |  +22%/+18ms | +27%/+22ms | +31%/+34ms | +33%/+56ms
512 |  +28%/+24ms | +31%/+28ms | +34%/+40ms | +35%/+64ms
(slot cols = 80ms, 160ms, 320ms, 480ms; entries format = "save/cost vs baseline% / delta p95 ms")

Recommended collateral and next steps:
- Create two 1-pagers for sales/solutions: (A) "MicroChat low-latency recipe" and (B) "Dedicated tiling ROI calculator" with an embedded slider for mean_seq and 95th-latency budget.
- Add a toggle in Console: preview predicted cost delta (percent) when switching tiling profile for a customer workload (using sampled production traces).
- Instrument an internal canary that flips one podpool to "tiling-optimized" and routes 5% of traffic for 48 hours; collect p50/p95 and egress of cold-eviction cases. JIRA: JIRA-OPT-387.

Appendix (raw observations):
- When slot>300ms we saw intermittent p99 spikes correlated with GPU kernel fallback followed by a 900ms GC-like pause in the runtime; root cause likely scheduling queue starvation under coalesced eviction.
- Prefetch aggressiveness needs dynamic throttling: we observed wasted KV fetches (~6% extra tokens fetched) in long-tail sessions when prefetch looked >2 chunks ahead.

Contacts for follow-up: Asha Patel (owner), Marco Delgado (bench infra), Jia Chen (cost model), Riley Thompson (SRE validation).

Unresolved questions for the team:
- Should we add a realtime estimator in the SDK that samples a short prefix and recommends tile size on the fly? (Pro: better per-app config; Con: added complexity and potential instability.)
- Pricing model: how deep should discounting be on Dedicated tiling-optimized SKUs? Current rough figure = 15% but requires finance sign-off.

Draft status: exploratory benchmark + annotated recommendations. Needs SRE runbook validation and a concise customer-facing one-pager before any release to console templates.
